title: Runtime Policy Decision Service + Lightweight Authorization Adapter with Enriched Audit
creator: Aisha Rahman
description: Design and implement a horizontally scalable Policy Decision Service (PDS) and a lightweight authorization adapter to be embedded in API runtime, console, and admin endpoints. The PDS provides fast, explainable authorization decisions, enriched audit attachments, and a migration path from RBAC v1 schemas. The adapter should be small, language-agnostic, and operate over gRPC/HTTP with best-effort caching and signed decision tokens for tamper-evident audit records.
technical_notes: PDS will expose a compact decision API: /v1/decide with input: subject, resource, action, context. Response must include: allow/deny, decision_id, reason_code, and optional explanation blob (compact JSON).

Implement two caching layers: 1) compiled policy AST cache (LRU, shared via in-memory local cache with configurable size) and 2) short-lived decision cache keyed by (subject, resource, action, stable-context-hash). Decision cache TTL default 200ms, configurable per route.
Policy language: adopt existing RBAC v2 DSL (YAML/JSON policies) and precompile into an optimized AST. Support partial evaluation for common prefixes and allow pre-warming for console admin flows.

Audit enrichment: PDS must emit structured audit entries to the audit-log pipeline with decision_id, policy_snapshot_version, requester_ip, request_headers (redacted), saml_user_claims (when present), and signed_decision_token (HMAC-SHA256) for later server-side verification.

Authz adapter: minimal dependency surface (single binary/library). Expose middleware for Go/Node/Python runtimes. Provide a sidecar adapter for legacy services that cannot link the library. Default to synchronous call; support async telemetry sampling for high-throughput routes.

SSO/SAML: admin console role mapping will read mapped attributes from SAML assertion (e.g., adminGroups). PDS must accept an optional saml_attributes bundle and validate attribute-to-role mapping according to customer-configured mappings.
Fallback behavior: when PDS is unavailable, adapter will rely on a conservative fallback policy (deny by default) but support a configurable emergency-open flag for on-call override with audit trail.

Performance targets: P95 decision latency <= 3ms on dedicated PDS instances with optimized kernels; P99 < 12ms. Throughput target 2k req/s per CPU core with batching disabled; enable lightweight batching for burst reduction.

Observability: emit decision_latency_ms, decision_cache_hit, policy_version, decision_result, saml_present, and signed_token_verified as metrics. Trace decisions with a span named pds.decision and include decision_id.

Backward compatibility: provide a migration shim that translates RBAC v1 role bindings to RBAC v2 policy nodes for 90% of existing use-cases; export a migration report for edge cases that require manual mapping.
Security: sign decision tokens using customer-managed key when running in Private mode; hosted mode uses Redwood KMS with key rotation and key_id included in audit events.
Testing: include a policy fuzzing harness, CI gating lint rules for policy schema, and golden decision tests for critical guarded endpoints (token creation, billing, admin toggles).
acceptance_criteria: PDS prototype deployed to staging with decision API and compiled policy cache working
Adapters implemented for Go and Node with middleware examples and integration tests
Audit pipeline receives enriched audit events including signed_decision_token and policy_snapshot_version
E2E test demonstrating SAML attribute-to-role mapping for admin console login
Performance verified against targets in staging (P95 <= 3ms) and documented perf run
Migration tool run against prod-like RBAC v1 dataset produces a report and automated mappings for >= 90% of bindings
Security review completed and documented; key handling approved for hosted and private deployments
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Canary): deploy PDS behind feature-flag for Platform and Console beta users (10% traffic). Collect latency, cache hit rate, and audit completeness.
Phase 2 (Expand): increment to 50% traffic and onboard adapters for non-critical runtime routes with deny-fallback disabled in test mode.
Phase 3 (Strict): enable adapters for critical routes with deny-by-default fallback and require signed_decision_token in audit stream.
Phase 4 (Migration): run RBAC v1->v2 migration tool for each org; open manual mapping tickets for unmapped bindings and schedule assisted remapping sessions.
Phase 5 (GA): enable PDS for all new tenants; provide rollout guide and CLI tools for customers to test policy changes safely (dry-run mode).
qa_steps: Unit tests for AST compiler and partial evaluator (coverage > 90%).
Integration tests: adapter <-> PDS over TLS with header redaction checks.
Fuzz tests for policy parser to ensure rejection of malformed inputs.
Load tests: synthetic workload matching peak patterns (short-churn admin checks + high-throughput embedding endpoints) to verify caching behavior.
Security tests: token signing verification, key rotation scenario, and SAML assertion replay tests.
DR test: simulate PDS outage and validate adapter fallback, alerting, and on-call override flows.
Manual review: console admin UX for mapping SAML attributes and the migration report review with PM and Customer Success.
notes: Design trade-off: prefer server-side PDS to centralize policy reasoning and make audits consistent, accepting an added network hop; mitigate with co-located cache and aggressive small TTLs.
Consider offering a library mode for high-security private installs where policy evaluation runs entirely in-process with signed proof exported for central audit collection.
Provide a low-code policy editor in Console for admins with built-in linting and dry-run against sampled requests before committing policy changes.
Coordinate with SRE for autoscaling rules and with Observability team to ensure decision traces are sampled at a configurable rate to limit cardinality.
